newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares ends firmer on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares ends firmer on overseas buying.

text.p: A wave of buying by overseas investors in Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) and a few heavyweight issues boosted overall market sentiment and spurred fresh buying across the board, brokers said on Tuesday.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 4.64 points, or 0.75 percent, to end at 620.81 points after falling to 615.67 points earlier as losers led gainers by 43 to 36 and 43 counters were unchanged.
Brokers said market sentiment was likely to become firmer on Wednesday as more overseas buyers were likely to take advantage of undervalued blue-chips.
"BNI and other banking stocks will remain a focus on Wednesday on continued fresh buying," a foreign broker said.
Newly-listed BNI topped the active list with 82.2 million shares, rising 75 rupiah to 1,275 rupiah, after hitting a high of 1,300 rupiah.
Brokers said the improved sentiment towards BNI was partly due to a recent report that the bank had cut its deposit rates by 50 basis points.
"I think some analysts made a new assesment of the stock following that news," a local broker said.
Brokers said the rise strengthened overall market sentiment and boosted other bank stocks including BDNI, Bank International Indonesia, Lippo Bank and Bank Danamon.
"Some investors were targeting other bank issues which have price earnings ratios close to that of BNI," one broker said.
BDNI rose 125 rupiah to 2,475 rupiah on a volume of 1.2 million shares, while Bank International Indonesia rose 75 rupiah to 2,275 on 3.4 million shares.
Blue-chip telecommunications firm Indosat rose to 6,400 rupiah before ending unchanged from its Monday close at 6,325 rupiah on a volume of 1.9 million shares on bargain-hunting, brokers said.
Telkom was also actively traded with 1.1 million shares at unchanged price of 3,925 rupiah after earlier touching a low of 3,900 rupiah on bargain-hunting, brokers said.

They said some big-capitalised stocks including pulp & paper producer Indah Kiat, cigarette firms Sampoerna and Gudang Garam as well as cement maker Semen Gresik were among the gainers on foreign buying.

Pulp & paper producer Indah Kiat of Sinar Mas Group rose 4.29 percent to 1,825 rupiah on a volume of 5.5 million shares on what brokers said was partly due to a recent report that the group would expand its pulp and paper business onto mainland China.
